summary: Klamath Peak lookout where Hallie Daggett, the first woman the Forest Service hired as a fire observer, worked from 1913; the register describes the 1958 metal tower as the existing structure.

facts.design: Metal tower with CL-10 metal cab, built 1958

Hallie Morse Daggett hired; first woman hired as a fire observer per the register
Daggett moved into the new lookout building in June 1925; register gives 1926
Daggett's last season at the station; a 1928 entry says she would not return
Existing metal tower with CL-10 metal cab
Nancy Culbertson took up the post soon after the tower went up; register credits her with 30 seasons
Interpretive trail honoring Daggett and Nancy Culbertson dedicated
Camera fire detection installed; lookout remained staffed in fire season

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1958 date is the current metal tower. The station began as a 1912 log cabin, was replaced by a cab dated 1925 or 1926, and a 1911 newspaper item already mentions a guard at the station.
The forest chronology has Daggett moving into the new building in June 1925, with completion reported in August 1925; the register says 1926. The story reports both.

sources.title: Hallie Daggett: A Woman of Uncommon Fortitude
sources.publisher: Prairie Rose Publications (Gail L. Jenner, blog)

notes_for_editor: History is well sourced from four pages. Current status is not: the latest staffing source is 2010 and no access rules were found, so no access or visit facts are recorded. The register gives elevation 6,483 ft while the Jenner blog gives 6,444 ft; neither is recorded in facts. The brief's conflict note says the record shares a register number with another entry; I did not check that other entry, and US 104 is what the register page shows. The 1925 vs 1926 cab date is flagged in the story, not corrected.
